topic: Sharp uniform minimax frontier for isotropic (distance-based) estimation along an assignment boundary in boundary discontinuity designs: prove the matching sup-norm converse carrying the logarithmic factor, so that the minimax risk over the distance-based class is of exact order (log n/n)^(1/4) on Cattaneo-Titiunik-Yu's nonparametric class with a uniform local-mass condition, and of exact order (log n/n)^(m/(2m+2)) with m = min(iota,q) on the sub-classes with uniformly regular C^(iota+2)-embedded support boundary; this settles their printed conjecture that the log^(1/4) n factor is unimprovable and supplies the first converse in the smooth-boundary regime.

open_problems.open_problem: Is the uniform minimax risk over Cattaneo-Titiunik-Yu's isotropic distance-based class, under a uniform local-mass condition along the assignment boundary, bounded below at exact order (log n/n)^(1/4)?

source_refs.claim: Their isotropic lower bound is only n^(-1/4), while their local-polynomial upper rate is (log n/n)^(1/4); they explicitly conjecture that the log^(1/4) n gap is unimprovable.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Rocio Titiunik, Ruiqi Rae Yu

source_refs.claim: For ordinary d-dimensional Holder regression, the global sup-norm minimax rate contains the logarithmic penalty (n/log n)^(-p/(2p+d)).
source_refs.author: Charles J. Stone

open_problems.why_unsolved: Cattaneo-Titiunik-Yu's converse uses an irregular rectifiable boundary to force n^(-1/4) error for every distance-only estimator, but it does not accumulate the many spatially separated hard alternatives that generate the extreme-value logarithm in classical global sup-norm lower bounds. A matching result must pack many boundary-local perturbations while simultaneously preserving rectifiability, the uniform local-mass condition, smooth bivariate regression functions, and indistinguishability after each sample is reduced to its distance from the evaluation point.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax theorem proving a constant-times (log n/n)^(1/4) lower bound for every isotropic distance-only estimator, paired with the existing local-polynomial upper bound to establish exact rate equivalence.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the causal estimand, explains why distance compression is empirically relevant, proves the existing one-point converse, and prints the exact conjecture to be closed.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Boundary discontinuity designs target a treatment-effect curve -> distance-only local polynomial methods incur geometry-driven uniform error -> the upper and lower minimax rates differ by log^(1/4) n -> prove that this logarithmic penalty is unavoidable.

method_exemplars.technique: Use a spatially distributed family of localized Holder perturbations and a multiple-testing minimax argument whose cardinality creates the global sup-norm logarithm.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired conclusion is precisely a Stone-type global sup-norm logarithmic converse, but restricted to experiments observed through the isotropic distance statistic.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct spline or wavelet alternatives for a matching sup-norm minimax lower bound, then couple the attaining estimator to a Gaussian process for uniform inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows how to preserve a nonstandard information restriction while making the lower-bound logarithm match a uniform estimator and confidence-band construction.

open_problems.open_problem: On uniformly regular C^(iota+2)-embedded assignment-boundary subclasses, is the exact isotropic sup-norm minimax rate (log n/n)^(m/(2m+2)), where m = min(iota,q)?

source_refs.claim: Their smooth-boundary theorem gives induced radial smoothness and uniform bias of order h^m, but their isotropic minimax converse is proved over the larger rectifiable class that may contain countably many kinks.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Rocio Titiunik, Ruiqi Rae Yu

source_refs.claim: The classical full-data Holder-regression benchmark gives the corresponding two-dimensional sup-norm exponent, but does not establish a converse for the distance-compressed experiment on an embedded boundary.
source_refs.author: Charles J. Stone

open_problems.why_unsolved: The available smooth-boundary result is an estimator-specific upper-bias calculation, whereas the available distance-only minimax lower bound obtains hardness by permitting nonsmooth geometry. A smooth-class converse must vary the embedded boundary and regression law within uniform derivative, reach or chart, density, and local-mass bounds, yet keep the induced distance experiments close enough while separating their boundary regression curves at the target sup-norm scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A lower-bound theorem over a uniformly regular C^(iota+2) boundary class at rate (log n/n)^(m/(2m+2)), together with an isotropic local-polynomial upper theorem at the same rate.

writing_exemplar.why: Its smooth-versus-kinked geometry narrative leads directly from the bias improvement to the missing smooth-class optimality statement.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Distance compression turns boundary geometry into radial smoothness -> a C^(iota+2) embedding restores m derivatives and h^m bias -> the resulting optimized upper rate has no distance-class converse -> establish the smooth-boundary minimax frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Balance Holder bump separation against likelihood information over a two-dimensional random design, using a sufficiently large packing to retain the sup-norm logarithm.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed exponent is the classical two-dimensional Holder exponent with effective smoothness m; the missing work is to realize that packing inside the distance-only boundary experiment.

method_exemplars.technique: Build uniformly regular embedded-manifold boundary alternatives and control their sampling mass and geometric separation in a nonasymptotic minimax argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its hard families preserve smooth embedded-boundary geometry, the central constraint absent from Cattaneo-Titiunik-Yu's kink-based converse.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze local-polynomial normal equations in intrinsic coordinates and prove that the estimator adapts to lower-dimensional manifold structure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The attaining side likewise needs a chart-uniform local-polynomial expansion whose rate is governed by induced geometry rather than ambient notation.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the sharp uniform minimax frontier for geometry-aware distance-based estimators that know finitely many kink locations or replace the assignment boundary by a controlled smooth approximation?

source_refs.claim: The paper recommends kink-aware bandwidth selection and notes that restricting estimation to smooth boundary segments avoids kink bias only by changing the target and adding regularization bias.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Rocio Titiunik, Ruiqi Rae Yu

source_refs.claim: Location-based local polynomial methods retain the bivariate score and avoid the irreducible kink bias suffered by distance-based methods, providing the full-information comparison benchmark.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Rocio Titiunik, Ruiqi Rae Yu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Geometry-aware trimming or smoothing changes both the effective bias and, potentially, the estimand near excluded kink neighborhoods. No existing theorem jointly optimizes stochastic error, ordinary radial approximation bias, and geometry-regularization bias, nor gives a converse showing when the procedure recovers the smooth-boundary rate and when information lost by distance compression still prevents it.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A rate characterization and matching lower bound indexed by kink number or smoothing radius, plus an explicit geometry-aware estimator and a uniform limit law for its regularized BATEC target.

writing_exemplar.why: Its conclusion lays out the geometry-aware intervention and the target-change tradeoff that should organize the new problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Kinks make radial regressions effectively nonsmooth -> known geometry can isolate locally smooth segments or define a smoothed boundary -> regularization lowers misspecification bias but alters the causal target -> characterize the optimal bias-risk frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Use local Voronoi geometry to locate boundary-near sample points and reconstruct smooth boundary pieces with explicit nonasymptotic error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a concrete way to quantify how accurately kink neighborhoods or smoothed boundary segments can be localized before regression.

method_exemplars.technique: Fit local polynomials in intrinsic neighborhoods and prove rate adaptation to manifold dimension without globally estimating the manifold.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A geometry-aware isotropic estimator similarly needs local chart information while retaining a simple local-polynomial construction.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply robust bias correction with pre-asymptotic Studentization and prove uniform Edgeworth and coverage-error expansions for local-polynomial intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once geometry regularization adds a new bias component, valid inference requires carrying its correction and variance effect through a nonstandard local-polynomial limit law.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a single data-driven distance-based procedure attain the sharp irregular-boundary and smooth-boundary sup-norm rates without knowing boundary regularity while also producing honest uniform confidence bands for the BATEC?

source_refs.claim: The paper supplies separate boundary-sensitive bandwidth rules and uniform bands, but does not establish sharp minimax adaptation with honest coverage across the irregular and smooth boundary classes.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Rocio Titiunik, Ruiqi Rae Yu

source_refs.claim: Honest adaptation across two distinct Holder balls is impossible without a nonparametric distinguishability condition; the paper gives a necessary-and-sufficient separation condition.
source_refs.author: Marc Hoffmann, Richard Nickl

source_refs.claim: For convex regression classes, data-dependent tuning cannot yield substantively shorter confidence intervals while retaining uniform coverage over the full class.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Michal Kolesar

open_problems.why_unsolved: The boundary-regularity index controls induced radial smoothness and therefore changes the optimal bandwidth and rate, but the observed experiment may not reliably distinguish a genuinely smooth boundary from an irregular boundary whose kink effects appear below the current resolution. General confidence-band theory says honest adaptation is impossible on unrestricted nested smoothness classes, so the boundary-discontinuity problem needs either a geometry-specific impossibility theorem or a concrete self-similarity or separation condition under which adaptation becomes feasible.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either an impossibility lower bound for honest rate adaptation across the two boundary classes, or a sufficient-condition theorem giving an adaptive estimator and honest uniform band with classwise sharp widths.

writing_exemplar.why: Its geometry-driven rate split is the natural motivation arc; the proposal can pivot from separate oracle regimes to the unresolved adaptive question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Boundary regularity determines induced radial smoothness -> the oracle bandwidth and sup-norm rate differ across kinked and smooth regimes -> regularity is not known in practice -> determine whether sharp estimation and honest bands can adapt.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine a Lepski-type adaptive resolution selector with a self-similarity restriction, and prove that the resulting band is simultaneously honest and rate-adaptive.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A boundary analogue of self-similarity could make smooth and kink-induced radial behavior statistically distinguishable at observable scales.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the ordered modulus of continuity over convex function classes to derive sharp confidence-length bounds and finite-sample optimal intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same modulus approach can quantify the unavoidable coverage-width cost of protecting against irregular boundaries while the truth is smooth.

method_exemplars.technique: Couple a multivariate Lipschitz-indexed empirical process uniformly to a Gaussian process with an explicit approximation rate, including multiplicative-separable classes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An adaptive boundary-discontinuity band needs a uniform Gaussian approximation valid over the data-dependent boundary locations and bandwidths selected by the procedure.

literature_map:
1. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu (2026, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2510.26051) establish distance-based BATEC identification, pointwise and uniform inference, an n^(-1/4) isotropic converse, and the printed log^(1/4) n conjecture.
2. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu (2026, arXiv:2505.05670) give the location-based full-bivariate-score benchmark and show that it avoids the distance method's irreducible kink bias.
3. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu (2026, arXiv:2511.06474) organize more than 80 boundary-discontinuity applications and distinguish location-, distance-, and pooling-based analyses.
4. Stone (1982, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/aos/1176345969) is the foundational global sup-norm Holder-regression rate result and supplies the classical logarithmic benchmark.
5. Korostelev (1993, Theory of Probability and Its Applications, DOI 10.1137/1138075) and Bertin (2004, Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference, DOI 10.1016/S0378-3758(03)00154-X) derive exact sup-norm minimax constants in fixed- and random-design regression.
6. Chen and Christensen (2018, Quantitative Economics, arXiv:1508.03365) match sup-norm lower and upper rates under an information-restricted inverse problem and construct uniform Gaussian and score-bootstrap bands.
7. Bickel and Li (2007, arXiv:0708.0983) prove that local polynomial regression can adapt to intrinsic manifold dimension without explicit global manifold estimation.
8. Cheng and Wu (2013, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2013.827984) analyze tangent-plane local linear regression and its geometric interpretation on manifolds.
9. Genovese, Perone-Pacifico, Verdinelli, and Wasserman (2012, JMLR, arXiv:1007.0549) develop smooth-manifold minimax lower constructions under Hausdorff loss.
10. Aamari, Aaron, and Levrard (2021, arXiv:2108.03135) give nonasymptotic minimax rates and a Voronoi boundary reconstruction procedure for smooth embedded manifolds with boundary.
11. Cattaneo and Yu (2025, arXiv:2406.04191) establish multivariate Lipschitz and multiplicative-separable empirical-process strong approximations used by the boundary-discontinuity uniform theory.
12. Cattaneo, Masini, and Underwood (2025, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2210.00362) provide Yurinskii couplings and feasible uniform inference for local-polynomial processes.
13. Calonico, Cattaneo, and Farrell (2022, Bernoulli, arXiv:1808.01398) provide uniform Edgeworth expansions and coverage-error-optimal robust bias-corrected local-polynomial inference.
14. Hoffmann and Nickl (2011, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1202.5145) and Bull (2012, Electronic Journal of Statistics, arXiv:1110.4985) identify distinguishability and self-similarity conditions needed for honest adaptive confidence bands.
15. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, Econometrica, arXiv:1511.06028) give sharp modulus-based optimal inference and an econometric impossibility benchmark for data-dependent tightening under uniform coverage.
